To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the purified (Na + K + )ATPase has an apparent turnover number of 3000 min −1 and that the phosphorylated intermediate is a 95,000 molecular weight polypeptide.
the purified (Na +,K + ) ATPase from the kidney medulla contains a single polypeptide chain of molecular weight of 110,000 and that this polypeptide chain is the phosphorylated intermediate.

the purified (Na + K + ) ATPase is phosphorylated on a specific aspartate residue in a reaction that is catalyzed by the enzyme and that this reaction occurs at a rate of approximately 3,000 molecules per second per enzyme molecule at 0 °C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification of the (Na ^{+} +K ^{+} ) adenosine 5′-triphosphatase and the characterization of this enzyme as a membrane protein.
the mechanism of action of the Na-K-ATPase.
the purification and reconstitution of the sodium and potassium dependent adenosine tri phosphatase from the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (Na + K + ) adenosinetrphosphatase is a phosphoprotein and is a dimer.

the (Na +K + )ATPase is a membrane-bound protein that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ATP in the presence of Na + and K + to produce ADP and inorganic phosphate, with concomitant transport of Na + and H + out of and K + into the cell, respectively.

the (Na + K + ) adenosinetriphosphatase of the kidney is a protein of molecular weight 110,000 composed of two polypeptides, one of molecular weight 95,000 and the other of molecular weight 50,000, and that the enzyme contains two sites for sodium and two sites for potassium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (Na +,K + ) ATPase is a phosphoprotein which undergoes a conformation change on phosphorylation.
the (Na +K + ) ATPase of renal medulla is composed of a large and a small polypeptide.
the (Na + K + )ATPase is a dimer of two subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphorylation is a very sensitive probe for the presence and activity of the (Na+ + K+) ATPase in the membrane.
the (Na + K + ) adenosinetriphosphatase is a very large molecule, and the turnover number is much less than that of the smaller molecules that are commonly studied.
the (Na + K + ) ATPase can be phosphorylated in a Na + -dependent manner.
